newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila sets targets, strategy for debt reduction.
newsitem.headline: Manila sets targets, strategy for debt reduction.

text.p: The Department of Finance has mapped out a strategy to reduce Philippine debt levels, according to a department report released on Wednesday.

The debt reduction targets, which will be presented to Congress, set debt repayments at 117.6 billion pesos in 1997, down from an estimated 133.5 billion pesos in 1996, and further down to 109.1 billion pesos in 1998, the report said.
As a percentage of gross national product, debt servicing is expected to drop to 4.6 percent in 1997 from 5.4 percent in 1996, and to 3.8 percent in 1998.

The strategy seeks to have a national government budget surplus running at more than 10 billion pesos yearly since a strong fiscal position leads to lower inflation and lower interest rates, the report said.
As part of the strategy, the government will continue to rely on cheaper official development assistance loans instead of commercial borrowing.
The government also aims to develop Philippine capital markets to further bring down interest rates.
